title: Additive-noise rigidity, a sharp growth threshold and an exact nonlinear-mixture boundary for Gaussian kernel spaces
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Kernel methods for random dynamical systems (kernel EDMD and kernel Koopman methods) often assume that the transition operator Tf(x) = E[f(X') | X = x] maps the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) of a Gaussian kernel boundedly into itself or into another Gaussian RKHS. An earlier Evidence Press release (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24089772) proved that, for transitions X' = F(x) + Z, this forces F to be affine when the characteristic function of the noise has a Gaussian lower bound, and asked whether that hypothesis can be removed and whether any state-dependent non-Gaussian transition can be admissible. This release answers both questions.

Results. (A) For every probability law of the noise Z, boundedness between global Gaussian RKHSs forces F to be injective and affine, and the operator norm has an exact formula; the noise enters only through a deterministic composition. (B) More generally, composition from a stationary source whose spectral measure dominates Lebesgue measure near zero into a Hilbert space of entire functions forces an affine map whenever the logarithm of the target's evaluation norm has zero exponential type in the imaginary direction; for every positive type there is a target admitting a bounded nonlinear map, so the condition is sharp. (C) A finite state-dependent mixture of Gaussian branches with a common linear part and fixed covariances is bounded exactly when each mixing probability extends to an entire function obeying an explicit Gaussian growth bound. With branch variance q, a bump gate exp(-αx2) qualifies exactly when α ≤ 8q/(1+4q); a probit gate Φ(βx) exactly when β2 ≤ 16q/(1+4q); a logistic gate never. (D) The same argument settles a several-variable case of the no-cancellation question for sums of weighted composition operators on Fock spaces.

Limits. The noise is formal at the operator level; the norm formula, multiplier criterion and smoothing spectrum are classical; the one-variable Fock no-cancellation statement was proved concurrently and more generally by Cho, Choe, Koo and Tien and by Lin, Lu, Yang and Zu. Results concern global RKHS norms only, not finite-data prediction. Branches with different linear parts, state-dependent covariances and general Markov transitions remain open.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF), the phase-diagram figure, three Python programs (verify.py: 97 checks; check_extensions.py: 63 checks at 50-digit precision; make_figures.py) with their JSON outputs, the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums.

Assurance. Written proofs with computational checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: a five-perspective Claude review panel, clean replays, one revision round with extensions, a re-review and a proof audit of new and rewritten proofs. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
